host:
Welcome to The Long and Short of It.
Today's contract debate topic is:
Will the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (FRED DGS10 official daily) print at or above 5.00% on any observation through Friday 23 Oct 2026 12:00 PM CT?

Affirmative will make the case for yes.
Negative will make the case for no.
yes:
Affirmative.

The long of it is that this time is the same machine that drove FRED DGS10 to its cycle high of 4.98% on October 19, 2023 — coupon supply plus TGA cash rebuild into QT — only now without the ON RRP cushion. Into that near-miss, Treasury had raised coupon auction sizes after the August 2, 2023 quarterly refunding while Fed SOMA Treasuries were still running off near 4.91 to 4.93 trillion dollars, and TGA balances climbed from 481.6 billion on September 6 to 841.1 billion by October 18. DGS10 never printed 5.00% then; the last official observation at or above 5.00% remains July 19, 2007. Fear is the buffer is gone: ON RRP that still sat above 2.2 trillion in May 2023 prints mostly under 1 billion day-to-day by early September 2026, while TGA sits near 944 billion and Fed total assets are already down to about 6.74 trillion. Soft-landing stories treat term premium as quiet; the captive-duration and fiscal-dominance narrative live on this site says coupon supply still has to clear without a wartime yield peg. Concession: the August 12, 2026 ten-year auction cleared with only 8.60% primary-dealer take-down and 76.73% indirect, versus 18.75% dealer take-down on October 11, 2023 — so if September 9 and October 7 ten-year allotments keep that non-dealer clearing, the rhyme can fail to push any official DGS10 print through 5.00% by October 23.
no:
Negative.

The short of it is that this time is different at the clearing margin and in US reserve-currency plumbing. The October 11, 2023 ten-year left 18.75% with primary dealers into the near-miss; the August 12, 2026 ten-year left only 8.60% with dealers and 76.73% with indirect bidders, and Fed custody on September 2, 2026 still shows about 2.60 trillion dollars of marketable Treasuries held for foreign official and international accounts. Hope is that this plumbing absorbs coupon supply the way an EM sudden-stop cannot — Thailand floated the baht on July 2, 1997, and the 1996 to 1997 reversal of net private capital flows across the five Asian crisis economies was about 11% of combined GDP. Soft-landing precedents in 1995 and 2019 kept expansions alive without a wartime two-and-a-half-percent long-bond peg; Japan ran yield-curve control from September 21, 2016 until March 19, 2024 with the Bank of Japan holding nearly half of JGBs, and the United States has had no standing yield ceiling since the 1951 Accord. Concession: debt held by the public is still near wartime scale — 98% of GDP in 2025 versus a 106% peak in 1946 — and ON RRP is drained, so a September 9 or October 7 ten-year allotment that pushes primary-dealer take-down back toward the October 2023 pattern would put the fiscal-dominance narrative back on trial. Until that print shows up, August clearing and foreign custody argue DGS10 stays below 5.00% through October 23.
close: This has been The Long and Short of It. Choose evidence over tribe.
